Velocidad de datos que pasa por el proxy: Data speed passing through the proxy right now: download (from the Internet to clients) and upload (from clients to the Internet). The chart shows the trend of the last few minutes.
Cuántas solicitudes HTTP procesó el prox: How many HTTP requests the proxy processed in the last minute. RPM = requests per minute. OK = served without denial; denied = blocked by access policy (403/407).
Direcciones IP distintas que generaron t: Distinct IP addresses that generated traffic in the last minute. "Authenticated" are those that sent a valid user: an IP can have traffic without a user (browser background noise), which is why these are different numbers.
Porcentaje de peticiones que Squid sirvi: Percentage of requests Squid served from its cache without going out to the Internet. Higher = less outgoing traffic and faster responses. "No cacheable requests" means there was no cacheable content, not that the cache is failing.
Resultado de las peticiones del último m: Result of the last minute's requests. Green (2xx) = successful. Blue (3xx) = redirects. Yellow (4xx) = client error or block. Red (5xx) = the server failed.
Velocidad de datos que pasa por el proxy: Data speed passing through the proxy over the last few minutes. Download = from the Internet to clients. Upload = from clients to the Internet. Each point is a sample taken every 5 seconds.
Quién consume más ancho de banda o hace: Who consumes the most bandwidth or makes the most requests. High consumption isn't necessarily a problem, but it's the first place to look if the link is slow or if a quota is worth reviewing.
Ordenado por datos transferidos · última: Sorted by data transferred · last 24 hours
Ordenado por número de peticiones · últi: Sorted by number of requests · last 24 hours
Qué dominios se piden más veces. Sirve p: Which domains are requested most often. Useful for deciding with real data whether a new ACL is worth adding: if something unproductive shows up here often, it's a candidate to block.
Por número de peticiones · últimas 24 ho: By number of requests · last 24 hours
Contra qué dominios está chocando la pol: Which domains the access policy is running into right now. If a domain repeats a lot, the rule blocking it is actually working, not just theory in the configuration.
Por número de bloqueos · últimas 24 hora: By number of blocks · last 24 hours
Quién insiste más contra la política. Un: Who pushes against the policy the most. A few blocks are normal noise (an old link, a redirect). A high, sustained count from the same person does warrant reviewing their access. It doesn't imply the account is disabled: denials can be due to old credentials or group policy.
Las peticiones más recientes registradas: The most recent requests recorded in Squid's access.log. Each row is a complete transaction: which IP made it, which user (if authenticated), which domain it went to, the response code, and how much data was transferred.
Direcciones IP desde las que navegó más: IP addresses that more than one distinct authenticated user browsed from. It's not a verdict -it can be a genuinely shared device (a meeting room, a kiosk)- but it's a signal worth reviewing: credentials shared between people look like this.
Quién llegó o pasó el límite de su cuota: Who has reached or gone over their browsing quota right now -by user or by group. Unlike the rest of this page, this doesn't depend on the time window chosen above: it's the current state, same as Management → Quotas manages it.

Uso libre para aplicaciones propias. Es: Free use for custom applications. It is the standard option for sending an application's logs to a SIEM: it is not mixed up with the operating system's messages. If in doubt, leave this one.
Uso libre, igual que local0. Sirve para: Free use, same as local0. It separates this source from other applications already using local0 on the same receiver.
Mensajes de programas de usuario en gene: Messages from user programs in general. Very generic: it gets mixed with other applications.
Servicios del sistema (demonios). Squid: System services (daemons). Squid is a daemon, but many receivers already reserve this label for the operating system itself.
Reservado para mensajes internos del pro: Reserved for the syslog service's own internal messages. Not suitable for a proxy.
Seguridad y autenticación. Úsalo solo si: Security and authentication. Use it only if the receiver treats these logs as security events.
Autenticación privada (acceso a cuentas): Private authentication (account access). Some receivers treat it as confidential.

It is not a verdict -it can be a genuinely shared machine (a room, a kiosk)-, but it is a signal worth checking: credentials circulating among people look like this. Each row shows since when and until when this was seen: it leaves the list once the chosen window passes without it happening again.

Unlike the rest of this page, this does not depend on the time window chosen above: it is the current state, as managed in Management → Quotas. A quota leaves this list when the reset date shown in each row arrives (or if the limit is raised or removed).
